questions.question_text: Which data type would best store the value 3.14159?
questions.explanation: double stores decimal (floating-point) numbers. int holds whole numbers, boolean true/false, char a single character. Pi needs a double for its fractional part.

questions.question_text: What does System.out.println(7 / 2.0); print?
questions.explanation: Because 2.0 is a double, the division promotes 7 to double too: 7/2.0 = 3.5. Mixing an int and a double yields a double result—unlike pure integer division (7/2 = 3).

questions.question_text: What does "Programming".substring(0, 4) return?
questions.explanation: substring(0, 4) takes indices 0,1,2,3 (end exclusive): 'P','r','o','g' = "Prog". The character at index 4 is not included.

questions.question_text: Which expression returns the length of String s?
questions.explanation: Strings use the length() METHOD (with parentheses). Arrays use the length FIELD (no parentheses), and ArrayLists use size(). Three different conventions to keep straight.

questions.question_text: What does this print? int x=5; if(x>0) if(x>10) System.out.print("A"); else System.out.print("B");
questions.explanation: The else pairs with the nearest if (x>10), which is false, so it prints 'B'. The 'dangling else' attaches to the closest unmatched if—a classic source of confusion.

questions.question_text: For booleans a=true, b=false, what is (a || b) && !(a && b)?
questions.explanation: (true || false) = true; (true && false) = false, so !(false) = true; true && true = true. This expression is XOR—true when exactly one operand is true.

questions.question_text: What does this loop print? for(int i=10; i>0; i-=3) System.out.print(i + " ");
questions.explanation: i decreases by 3: 10, 7, 4, 1; at i=-2 the condition i>0 fails. Trace the decrementing sequence—the loop stops once i is no longer positive.

questions.question_text: Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least once?
questions.explanation: A do-while checks its condition AFTER running the body, so it always executes once. while and for check before, possibly running zero times. (Note: do-while isn't on the AP exam but the concept clarifies loop behavior.)

questions.question_text: Method overloading means having multiple methods with the same name but:
questions.explanation: Overloaded methods share a name but differ in parameter number or types (e.g., print(int) vs print(String)). Differing only in return type isn't valid overloading—the parameters distinguish them.

questions.question_text: Why is it good practice to make instance variables private?
questions.option_b: to enforce encapsulation, controlling access through methods
questions.explanation: Private fields hide internal state and force access through controlled methods (getters/setters), protecting object invariants. This encapsulation is a core OOP principle.

questions.question_text: What is printed? int[] a={5,10,15}; System.out.println(a.length);
questions.explanation: length is the number of elements (3), accessed as a field without parentheses. Don't confuse the length (3) with the last index (2) or the values stored.

questions.question_text: After this swap, what is arr? int[] arr={1,2,3}; int t=arr[0]; arr[0]=arr[2]; arr[2]=t;
questions.explanation: The temp variable t preserves arr[0]=1 while arr[0] becomes 3 and arr[2] becomes 1: {3,2,1}. Using a temporary is the standard way to swap without losing a value.

questions.question_text: What does list.get(0) return for an empty ArrayList?
questions.explanation: An empty list has no index 0, so get(0) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException. Always check size() before accessing elements to avoid this runtime error.

questions.question_text: What does this leave list as? ArrayList<Integer> list=new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList(1,2,3)); list.add(1, 99);
questions.explanation: add(1, 99) inserts 99 at index 1, shifting 2 and 3 right: [1, 99, 2, 3]. The two-argument add inserts at a position rather than appending to the end.

questions.question_text: How do you set the element in row 1, column 0 of int[][] grid to 7?
questions.explanation: 2D access is grid[row][column], so row 1 column 0 is grid[1][0]. Java uses separate bracket pairs, not comma syntax, and the order is row first.

questions.question_text: What does this count? int[][] m={{1,0},{1,1}}; int c=0; for(int[] r:m) for(int v:r) if(v==1) c++;
questions.explanation: It counts elements equal to 1: row {1,0} has one, row {1,1} has two = 3 total. The nested enhanced for visits every cell, incrementing on each match.

questions.question_text: If class B extends A and both have a method show(), calling show() on a B object runs:
questions.explanation: The actual object's type (B) determines which override runs—dynamic dispatch picks B's show(). To call A's version from within B, use super.show().

questions.question_text: An interface in Java primarily defines:
questions.option_b: a set of method signatures that implementing classes must provide
questions.explanation: An interface specifies methods a class must implement, enabling polymorphism across unrelated classes (e.g., Comparable). It's a contract of behavior, traditionally without implementation bodies.

questions.question_text: What does this return? int f(int n){ if(n<=1) return n; return f(n-1)+f(n-2);} f(4)
questions.explanation: This is Fibonacci: f(4)=f(3)+f(2)=(f(2)+f(1))+(f(1)+f(0))=(1+1)+(1+0)... computing: f(0)=0,f(1)=1,f(2)=1,f(3)=2,f(4)=3. The two base cases (n=0,1) anchor the recursion.

questions.question_text: A recursive method without progress toward its base case will cause:
questions.explanation: If each call doesn't move closer to the base case, recursion never stops and the call stack overflows. Ensuring progress (like n-1) toward the base case is essential to correct recursion.

questions.question_text: What is the value of 10 % 3 + 3 % 10?
questions.explanation: 10 % 3 = 1 (remainder of 10÷3); 3 % 10 = 3 (since 3 < 10, the whole 3 is the remainder). Sum = 1 + 3 = 4. When the dividend is smaller, modulus returns the dividend itself.

questions.question_text: What does "hello".charAt(1) return?
questions.explanation: charAt(1) returns the char at index 1, which is 'e' (h=0, e=1). It returns a char (single quotes), not a String—a subtle type distinction.

questions.question_text: Which operator checks equality of two int values?
questions.explanation: == compares primitive values (and object references). A single = is assignment; .equals() compares object contents; != is 'not equal'. For ints, use ==.

questions.question_text: What does this compute? int n=0; for(int i=1;i<=100;i++) if(i%5==0) n++; System.out.println(n);
questions.explanation: It counts multiples of 5 from 1 to 100: 5,10,...,100 = 100/5 = 20 numbers. The i%5==0 test identifies each multiple, incrementing the counter.

questions.question_text: A mutator (setter) method typically:
questions.option_b: changes the value of a private field
questions.explanation: Mutators modify instance variables (often with validation), while accessors (getters) return values. Together they provide controlled access to private fields—encapsulation in practice.

questions.question_text: Which declares and initializes an array of 5 integers all set to 0?
questions.explanation: new int[5] creates a 5-element int array auto-initialized to 0. Java requires 'new' with a size; {5} would make a 1-element array holding 5, and the other syntaxes are invalid.

questions.question_text: Polymorphism allows a single variable of a superclass type to:
questions.option_b: reference objects of different subclasses and call their overridden methods
questions.option_c: change its type at compile time
questions.explanation: A superclass reference can point to any subclass object, and method calls dispatch to the actual object's override at runtime. This is the power of polymorphism—uniform handling of varied types.

questions.question_text: The part of a recursive method that does NOT call itself and stops the recursion is the:
questions.explanation: The base case provides a direct answer without further recursion, ending the chain. The recursive case reduces the problem and calls the method again toward that base case.
